mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above the 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand but expanding construction activity, which historically precedes a mild negative equity correction over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately driving higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to a financial shock, which typically boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 3% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% over two months signals a precautionary savings behavior, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as consumers delay discretionary spending.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA AND GDPC1 < 12-month MA -1% over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which typically sustains positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days by boosting corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 12-month moving averages for three months signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA AND HOUST < 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 95% confidence.
